abstract: Plasma extracellular vesicles (EVs) are promising liquid biopsy biomarkers, yet their proteomic profiling remains confounded by massive co-isolation. Here, we resolve this heterogeneity through a meta-analysis of 515 human plasma EV proteomes. We demonstrate that the reproducible core proteome is overwhelmingly governed by predictable, surface-charge-driven mass-action that dynamically mirrors synthetic nanoparticle corona formation. By quantitatively decomposing the core isolate against pan-synthetic coronas and agonist-induced platelet EVs, we trace the core isolate to three main mechanistic origins: an electrostatic plasma corona, ex vivo platelet vesiculation and biological macromolecular co-isolates. Crucially, the residual vesicular cargo strongly correlates with thrombin-induced platelet degranulation, indicating that phlebotomy-induced trauma contribute to the bulk signal. We provide a modular atlas that mathematically distinguishes biophysical coronas from these cellular co-isolates, establishing a new framework for interpreting biological origin in plasma EV proteomics.
